title: Write your own core
lede: Describe your own core in a core manifest, give it a microarchitecture package, select it and test it.
prerequisites: The tools from [Install tools and run a simulation](#/guides/getting-started#1-install-the-tools). The Spike stage also needs Spike's headers and libraries.
A SoC manifest, as in [Build a SoC and run a program on it](#/tutorials/instantiate-core).
outcome: A tile that your SoC manifest can select, a passing connection test, and the steps to compare its executed instructions with Spike.

stages.title: Read what a tile must connect to
stages.text: A tile is a core plus whatever sits between it and memory. Every tile has the same ports: an instruction channel and a data channel to the memory fabric, interrupt inputs, and halt and flush signals.

stages.title: Describe the core
stages.text: A core manifest lists the core's source files and its top module. It also requests the compiler ISA and microarchitecture settings. Prism generates package headers and checks the requested ISA against the elaborated hardware. A tile manifest selects the core by naming the core manifest.

stages.title: Implement the tile ports
stages.text: Write the tile module that connects your core's own memory bus to the two channels.

stages.title: Test the connection
stages.text: Name the new core in a tile manifest, name that tile in your SoC manifest, then lint it and run the connection test.

stages.title: Compare with Spike
stages.text: Report each completed instruction from your core. Prism then runs the same program on Spike and compares the two instruction by instruction.

stages.title: Run firmware
stages.text: To receive programs through the ROM loader, your core must support what the loader uses. The core manifest states what the core supports.

stages.title: Synthesize and run gate-level simulation
stages.text: Add the entry points that let Prism synthesize your core on its own, then compare the synthesized netlist with the RTL.
